#### Which covariate should be adjusted

<!-- generated-learning-note -->
This subsection explains **Which covariate should be adjusted** and shows how it contributes to the overall Which covariate should be adjusted workflow.


In this example, we assume to investigate the causality between smoking and mortality:  whether smoking will more likely cause mortality. We collect the following variables. 

![](C:\Users\hed2\Downloads\mybook2\mybook2\dagitty-smoke dots.jpg) 

Smoking is the exposure, Mortality is the outcome, and others are patient confounders.


Then, we connect these knots by directed arrow according to our domain knowledge. It is called as directed acyclic graph (DAG).

![](C:\Users\hed2\Downloads\mybook2\mybook2\dagitty-smoke.jpg) 

We also can add unobserved variables into this graph, like Sport. The blue knots indicate the mediators, and the red ones are confounders which we need to adjust. If the purpose is to investigate the overall effect of smoking and mortality, we should not adjust the blue knots.

After adjusted these confounders, we can get the average total effect between 
them.

![](C:\Users\hed2\Downloads\mybook2\mybook2\dagitty-smoke after adjusting.jpg)

**`Minimal sufficient adjustment sets for estimating the total effect of Smoking on Mortality:
Age, Alcohol, Psychosocial, Sex`**

Using the [DAGitty tool](http://www.dagitty.net) ([Tutor](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3euqrnD9w7c&list=PLS6tnpTr39sFEzQGpWVT-K775iKbj5Bbp&index=2)), we can see that "There are no instruments or conditional instruments in this DAG" and "The direct effect cannot be estimated by covariate adjustment".

Please notice we still can not adjust those unobserved variables and unconsidered factors by using this tool.

## Interpreting the Results

Check timing, coding, measurement quality, missingness, and the causal role of each candidate covariate. Treat the output as evidence generated under the stated data, coding choices, and assumptions. Before using the workflow in practice, replace example inputs with validated data and confirm that the method targets the intended scientific question.

## Key Takeaways

- **Connect method to purpose.** Identify the question and target quantity before choosing code or a model.
- **Read code and output together.** Confirm what each object, estimate, interval, table, or plot represents.
- **Check assumptions and diagnostics.** A successful computation is not by itself evidence that the result is reliable.
- **Adapt deliberately.** When applying the example elsewhere, document changes to data definitions, parameters, and analytical choices.
